fact: The BCEAO told every bank, e-money issuer and payment institution in the eight WAEMU states, Niger included, in April 2026 to be connected to PI-SPI by 30 June 2026, then on 25 June 2026 moved the deadline to 30 September 2026 (microfinance institutions 30 June 2027), according to iAfrikan.
The UMOA Banking Commission's 2025 report, as relayed by Horonya Finance, counts one licensed e-money issuer (EME, a non-bank) in Niger at 31 December 2025, among 18 across the Union.

Finance SAO reports the BCEAO communique of 25 June 2026 set 30 September 2026 as the new deadline to integrate with PI-SPI for banks, e-money institutions and payment institutions in the UEMOA, Niger included, and 30 June 2027 for microfinance institutions.
L'Oeil du Sahel reports that the BCEAO's 2 October 2026 communique, covering Niger as a UEMOA state, sets binding rules for interoperable e-money transfers from 2 November 2026.
L'Oeil du Sahel reports that the BCEAO communique requires interoperable e-money transfers in UEMOA, including Niger, to be routed through PI-SPI from 2 November 2026.
L'Oeil du Sahel cites the UMOA banking commission as recording Airtel Money Niger with 1.311 billion FCFA of capital and 4.605 billion FCFA of e-money outstanding at end 2024.
